Subject: Clarify prefix granularity & minimums for pilot billing

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're prepping the internal cost model for the Acme pilot and two billing items are ambiguous on our side: prefix deduplication (when repeated prompts reuse a cached prefix) and the per-request minimum/rounding rules for short calls.

Concrete asks:
- When two requests within the same session share an identical 120-token prefix but different suffixes, how are tokens billed? Do you bill the full 120 each call, only the delta, or something in between?
- What's the per-request minimum (if any) and what quantum do you round to for streaming responses? Acme's procurement needs line-item certainty for their monthly estimate.

I've attached two sample pilot invoices (pilot_sample_invoices.pdf) showing current expectations from our billing team. Can you loop in finance/technical ops so we can finalize reconciliation rules before we sign the SOW?

Hi Sam / Logan — thanks for the detail. Below are the exact rules we apply for the hosted billing SKU used in the Acme pilot, plus two short worked examples. I tried to keep the language procurement-friendly so you can paste it into your cost sheet. The team discussion can focus on the line-item labels.

1) Prefix deduplication (cache-aware billing)
- When multiple requests in the same session share an identical prefix that is satisfied from an active KV/prefix cache, we do NOT bill the cached tokens again. Only newly generated or non-cached input tokens are billed for that request.
- Cache window: 45 seconds of inactivity resets the prefix cache for billing purposes.
- Example A (prefix reuse):
  * Request 1: 120-token prompt prefix + 80-token suffix => billed input tokens = 200 (120 prefix counted once). Output = 150 tokens => billed output tokens = 150.
  * Request 2 (within 30s, identical 120-token prefix + new 50-token suffix): billed input tokens = 50 (only the new suffix) + billed output tokens = 120.
  * Net billed tokens across both calls = 200 + 150 + 50 + 120 = 520 tokens (we do not double-count the 120 cached prefix).

2) Per-request minimums and rounding quantum
- Per-request minimum: 20 tokens per request (input+output combined). If a single request's total billed tokens < 20, we invoice a 20-token minimum for that request.
- Rounding quantum for invoices: we round billed tokens up to the nearest 10-token quantum on the invoice to reduce noise from microcalls. Rounding happens after prefix deduplication and before summing across the billing period.
- Example B (small call):
  * Short request: billed tokens (post-dedup) = 7 -> apply 20-token minimum -> invoice records 20 tickets -> then rounding to nearest-10 keeps it at 20.

3) Streaming responses and partial token handling
- For streaming responses we accumulate tokens emitted and apply the same minimum/rounding rules at request-completion. If a stream is interrupted and reconnected within the same session, we look to the stream metadata to deduplicate already-received tokens where possible.

4) Credits & pilot smoothing
- For pilots we commonly apply a one-time smoothing credit if early invoices differ from final expected usage by >15%. We can set a provisional credit cap (e.g., $5k) tied to the pilot term.

Attachments: I've dropped a short billing playbook (billing-playbook-v2.pdf) with annotated invoice rows (recommended invoice line names: "Redwood inference - tokens (input)" and "Redwood inference - tokens (output)").

If that aligns, we can:
- Confirm invoice line-item text you need for GL mapping.
- Offer the smoothing credit as part of the SOW appendix
- Kick off the Thursday call if that works for your team.

Thanks,
